001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.simple.props;
002
003import java.io.IOException;
004import java.io.InputStream;
005import java.io.StringReader;
006import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
007import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
008import java.util.List;
009import java.util.Objects;
010import java.util.function.Function;
011
012import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
013
014import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProperties;
015
016/**
017 * Resolves {@link LogProperties} from up to three layers, highest priority first:
018 * <ol>
019 * <li>System properties
020 * ({@link LogProperties.StandardProperties#SYSTEM_PROPERTIES}).</li>
021 * <li>Environment variables, using {@value Builder#DEFAULT_ENV_PREFIX} (configurable) in
022 * place of the {@code "logging."} lead segment of the key, remaining <code>.</code>s
023 * replaced with <code>_</code>, and casing left exactly as-is - see
024 * {@link Builder#envPrefix(String)}.</li>
025 * <li>A classpath resource (default {@value Builder#DEFAULT_RESOURCE}, configurable)
026 * parsed the same way {@link LogProperties.Builder#fromProperties(String)} parses any
027 * other properties text - if the resource is not found this layer contributes
028 * nothing.</li>
029 * </ol>
030 * Create one with {@link #builder()}, or just rely on {@link SimplePropertiesProvider}
031 * picking up the defaults automatically via {@link java.util.ServiceLoader}.
032 * <p>
033 * <b>GraalVM native image</b>: this module bundles a {@code resource-config.json} (at
034 * {@code META-INF/native-image/io.jstach.rainbowgum/rainbowgum-simple-props/}) that
035 * registers the default resource name, {@value Builder#DEFAULT_RESOURCE}, so a
036 * {@code logging.properties} on the classpath is included in the native image
037 * automatically - native-image's own embedded-configuration discovery picks this up from
038 * any jar on the build classpath, no extra plugin or flag needed. A custom
039 * {@link Builder#resource(String)} is a different resource name, so it is <em>not</em>
040 * covered by that file - add your own {@code resource-config.json} entry (or pass
041 * {@code -H:IncludeResources=...} directly) for it.
042 */
043public final class SimpleProperties {
044
045        private final List<LogProperties> properties;
046
047        private SimpleProperties(List<LogProperties> properties) {
048                this.properties = properties;
049        }
050
051        /**
052         * The three layers described in this class's javadoc, highest priority first.
053         * @return properties, highest priority first.
054         */
055        public List<LogProperties> properties() {
056                return properties;
057        }
058
059        /**
060         * Creates a builder.
061         * @return builder.
062         */
063        public static Builder builder() {
064                return new Builder();
065        }
066
067        /**
068         * Builds a {@link SimpleProperties}.
069         */
070        public static final class Builder {
071
072                /**
073                 * Default environment variable prefix: {@value #DEFAULT_ENV_PREFIX}.
074                 */
075                public static final String DEFAULT_ENV_PREFIX = "RAINBOWGUM_";
076
077                /**
078                 * Default classpath resource: {@value #DEFAULT_RESOURCE}.
079                 */
080                public static final String DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "classpath:/logging.properties";
081
082                private String envPrefix = DEFAULT_ENV_PREFIX;
083
084                private String resource = DEFAULT_RESOURCE;
085
086                private Function<String, @Nullable String> envLookup = System::getenv;
087
088                private Builder() {
089                }
090
091                /**
092                 * Sets the environment variable prefix used in place of the key's
093                 * {@code "logging."} lead segment (for example {@code logging.level.root} becomes
094                 * {@code RAINBOWGUM_level_root} with the default prefix). Casing is not touched -
095                 * only the prefix and the remaining <code>.</code>-to-<code>_</code> replacement
096                 * are applied - so a key with mixed-case segments produces a mixed-case
097                 * environment variable name.
098                 * @param envPrefix prefix, default {@value #DEFAULT_ENV_PREFIX}.
099                 * @return this.
100                 */
101                public Builder envPrefix(String envPrefix) {
102                        this.envPrefix = Objects.requireNonNull(envPrefix);
103                        return this;
104                }
105
106                /**
107                 * Sets the classpath resource to load properties from. A leading
108                 * {@code classpath:} scheme (with or without a following <code>/</code>) is
109                 * stripped before resolving; the remainder is resolved as a plain classpath
110                 * resource name. Not found is not an error - that layer simply contributes no
111                 * properties.
112                 * @apiNote unlike the default resource name, a custom one here is not covered by
113                 * this module's bundled GraalVM {@code resource-config.json} - see this class's
114                 * javadoc.
115                 * @param resource classpath resource, default {@value #DEFAULT_RESOURCE}.
116                 * @return this.
117                 */
118                public Builder resource(String resource) {
119                        this.resource = Objects.requireNonNull(resource);
120                        return this;
121                }
122
123                /*
124                 * Test-only hook so env var mapping can be tested without setting real
125                 * environment variables (which the JVM cannot do portably at test time).
126                 */
127                Builder envLookup(Function<String, @Nullable String> envLookup) {
128                        this.envLookup = Objects.requireNonNull(envLookup);
129                        return this;
130                }
131
132                /**
133                 * Builds the {@link SimpleProperties}.
134                 * @return simple properties.
135                 */
136                public SimpleProperties build() {
137                        var systemProperties = LogProperties.StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES;
138                        var environmentVariables = new EnvVarProperties(envPrefix, envLookup);
139                        var classpathProperties = loadResource(resource);
140                        return new SimpleProperties(List.of(systemProperties, environmentVariables, classpathProperties));
141                }
142
143                private static LogProperties loadResource(String resource) {
144                        String path = resource;
145                        if (path.startsWith("classpath:")) {
146                                path = path.substring("classpath:".length());
147                        }
148                        while (path.startsWith("/")) {
149                                path = path.substring(1);
150                        }
151                        ClassLoader cl = SimpleProperties.class.getClassLoader();
152                        if (cl == null) {
153                                cl = Thread.currentThread().getContextClassLoader();
154                        }
155                        try (InputStream in = cl == null ? null : cl.getResourceAsStream(path)) {
156                                if (in == null) {
157                                        return LogProperties.StandardProperties.EMPTY;
158                                }
159                                String content = new String(in.readAllBytes(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
160                                return SimpleLogProperties.read(new StringReader(content), resource);
161                        }
162                        catch (IOException e) {
163                                throw new UncheckedIOException("Failed to read classpath resource: " + resource, e);
164                        }
165                }
166
167        }
168
169}
